record.title: Frobenius formula for shifted square sequences beyond 30
record.statement:
Let $a$ be an integer with $a>30$, and let

$$
A(a)=(a,a+1^2,a+2^2,a+3^2,\ldots).
$$

Let $S(A(a))$ be the numerical semigroup generated by $A(a)$. For $n\in\mathbb{Z}^{+}$, let $\iota(n)$ be the least number of positive integral squares whose sum is $n$. **Frobenius formula for shifted square sequences.** For every integer $a>30$, the hypotheses of the preceding theorem are satisfied, and consequently

$$
F(S(A(a)))=3a+\max\{r\mid 1\leq r\leq a-1,\ \iota(r)=4,\ \iota(a+r)\geq 3,\ \iota(2a+r)\geq 2\}.
$$

This gives an explicit formula for the Frobenius number of the numerical semigroup generated by the shifted square sequence when the initial parameter exceeds $30$; the supplied text does not indicate whether this assertion has been independently proved or remains open.
record.source_name: Kyunghwan Song, “The Frobenius problem for shifted square sequences”, arXiv:2605.25542 (2026).

record.title: Cha's simplicial-polytope conjecture for arbor h-polynomials
record.statement: Let $E$ be an $n$-element set and let $\tau$ be an arbor on $E$. Its $h$-polynomial is $h(\tau,t)=\sum_{i=0}^n h_i(\tau)t^i$, where $h_i(\tau)$ counts the lattice points of the arbor polytope $\mathcal Q_\tau$ having $i$ nonzero coordinates. **Cha's simplicial-polytope conjecture.** The polynomial $h(\tau,t)$ is equal to the $h$-polynomial of an $n$-dimensional simplicial polytope for every arbor $\tau$ on $E$. In particular, $h(\tau,t)$ is palindromic and unimodal. This is attributed to Cha (2025); its resolution is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Frédéric Chapoton and Christos A. Athanasiadis, “Polytopes and posets associated to preorders”, arXiv:2605.26916 (2026).

record.title: Weak Harris–Morrison slope conjecture
record.statement:
For each integer $g$, let $s_g$ denote the slope of the effective cone of divisors of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$, the moduli space of stable curves of genus $g$.

**Weak Harris–Morrison slope conjecture.** For every $g$,

$$
s_g>6.
$$

The original Harris–Morrison upper-bound conjecture was disproved, but the weaker inequality above is consistent with the known results and remains open in general. In the paper it is used to obtain uniqueness of the partition functions of certain holomorphic VOAs of central charge $24$.
record.source_name: Sebastiano Carpi and Giulio Codogni, “Vertex operator algebras, partition functions and Teichmüller modular forms”, arXiv:2605.26972 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26972

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2026). “This is a very important conjecture in the theory of vertex operator algebras which is still open, see Section .”

record.title: Ding–Zhao's revised adjacent Ruzsa-number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $R_m$ be the Ruzsa number of the residue class ring $\mathbb Z_m$, namely the least integer $r$ for which a subset has between $1$ and $r$ ordered representations of every residue as a sum of two elements. **Ding–Zhao's revised conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $m$, we have

$$
\big|R_{m+1}-R_m\big|\le 1.
$$

The revised statement excludes the finitely many computed exceptions, including $R_{36}=6$ and $R_{37}=4$. The source presents it as an open conjecture based on computations through $m=100$.
record.source_name: Yuchen Ding, Huixi Li, Junfeng Li, Wei Niu and Xiamiao Zhao, “Adjacent comparison bounds and extremal sets for Ruzsa numbers”, arXiv:2606.11069 (2026).

record.title: Global PCL-indexability of discounted single-project problems
record.statement:
Let $p_{01}$, $\rho$, $\kappa$, and $\beta$ be parameters satisfying

$$
0<p_{01}<1,\qquad 0<\rho<1-p_{01},\qquad 0<\kappa<1,\qquad 0<\beta<1.
$$

A discounted single-project problem is PCL-indexable when the conditions $\textup{(PCLI1)--(PCLI3)}$ hold on the full threshold range. **Global PCL-indexability.** For every feasible parameter tuple satisfying the displayed inequalities, the discounted single-project problem is PCL-indexable.

The conjecture extends the analytically tractable PCL-indexability results to the unresolved intermediate threshold regime. Numerical experiments found no counterexamples on extensive parameter grids, but a complete analytical verification remains open.
record.source_name: José Niño-Mora, “Restless bandits with imperfect binary feedback: PCL-indexability analysis and computation”, arXiv:2606.11192 (2026).

record.title: Bruhat-order monotonicity conjecture for the function $f_n$
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak A_n$ denote the alternating group, let $f_n$ be the function defined by the paper's Algorithm 1, and let $\leq$ denote the Bruhat order on $\mathfrak A_n$. **Bruhat-order conjecture.** For all $n$ and all $w\in\mathfrak A_n$, one has

$$
w\leq f_n(w)
$$

in the Bruhat order.

The conjecture extends the verified result for $n\leq 13$; the inversion-number inequality $\operatorname{inv}(w)<\operatorname{inv}(f_n(w))$ is known for every nonidentity $w$, but the full Bruhat-order assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Sihong Pan, Mark Skandera and Jiayuan Wang, “Permanental Inequalities and Unit Interval Orders”, arXiv:2606.13162 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: Hilton's cycle multiplicity conjecture for dense hamiltonian graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$) be a hamiltonian graph of order $n$, and let $e(G)$ denote its number of edges and $c_\ell(G)$ the number of cycles of length $\ell$ in $G$. Assume

$$
e(G) > \left\lfloor \frac{n^2}{4} \right\rfloor + 1.
$$

**Hilton's conjecture.** For every integer $\ell$ with $3\le \ell\le n$,

$$
c_\ell(G) \ge n-\ell+2.
$$

The conjecture strengthens Sheehan's theorem, which guarantees at least two cycles of every length under the same density condition. It is known at the endpoint $\ell=n$, and the triangle case follows from a result of Erdős; the full conjecture has remained open since 1977, although the paper proves it for sufficiently large order and leaves only finite exceptional ranges for lengths $6\le \ell\le 10$.
record.source_name: Chengli Li, Leyou Xu and Bo Zhou, “The number of cycles of a given length in dense hamiltonian graphs: proving Hilton's conjecture”, arXiv:2606.16114 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16114

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

record.title: Parity conjecture for the unique invariant theta characteristic on modular curves
record.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime with $p\geq 7$, and let $X(p)$ denote the modular curve of level $p$. An **invariant theta characteristic** is a theta characteristic on $X(p)$ invariant under the relevant group action.

**Parity conjecture.** The unique invariant theta characteristic on $X(p)$ is always even.

This conjecture extends the computations for $p=7,11,13,17$, where the unique invariant theta characteristic was found to be even. The parity for all odd primes $p\geq 7$ remains open.
record.source_name: Linden Disney-Hogg, “The Parity of Invariant Characteristics”, arXiv:2606.20938 (2026).
record.references:
**7 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2507.00860](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00860), [arXiv:2208.11616](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.11616), [arXiv:2207.02509](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02509), [arXiv:2105.06574](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.06574), [arXiv:1011.2991](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.2991), [arXiv:1002.0554](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.0554).

record.title: Even-degree tautological cohomology conjecture for moduli spaces of curves
record.statement:
Let $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ be the moduli space of stable curves, let $H^k(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n})$ denote its cohomology, and let $RH^k(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n})$ denote the corresponding tautological cohomology. **Even-degree tautological cohomology conjecture.** For every even $k\leq 20$ and all $g,n$, one has

$$
H^k(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n})=RH^k(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}).
$$

The claim is motivated by the expectation that even cohomology in this range is pure Tate, while known non-tautological algebraic cycles occur in degrees at least $22$; the source does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Hannah Larson, “Chow rings, cohomology rings, and point counts of moduli spaces of curves”, arXiv:2606.29656 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29656

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2026). “We refer the reader to the excellent survey article for a description of these tautological relations, their history, and open questions about them.”

record.title: The MMS conjecture on non-negative sums in sampling without replacement
record.statement:
Fix integers $n\ge 2$ and $k<n$. Let $\mathcal{N}_n$ be the family of multisets $P=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$ of real numbers satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=0$. Choose $\mathbb{I}\in\binom{[n]}{k}$ uniformly at random and define

$$
X_P=\sum_{i\in\mathbb{I}}x_i.
$$

**MMS conjecture.** If $n\ge 4k$, then for every $P\in\mathcal{N}_n$,

$$
\mathbb{P}(X_P\ge 0)\ge \frac{k}{n}.
$$

The bound is sharp for the population consisting of one element equal to $1$ and $n-1$ elements equal to $-1/(n-1)$. The conjecture is open in general; the best stated upper bound in the source is $N_k\le 10^{46}k$, where $N_k$ is the least integer such that the inequality holds for all $n\ge N_k$ and all $P\in\mathcal{N}_n$.
record.source_name: Jianhang Ai, Ondřej Kuželka and Christos Pelekis, “An entropic analogue of the MMS conjecture”, arXiv:2606.30486 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30486

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

record.title: The equivariant Schur Lam–Postnikov–Pylyavskyy inequality
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be partitions, let $\mathbf x_k=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$, and let $s_\lambda(\mathbf x_k;\mathbf y)$ denote the double Schur polynomial. Write $\lambda\vee\mu$ and $\lambda\wedge\mu$ for the join and meet of the two partitions, and interpret $\leq_s^{\mathrm{equiv}}$ as the equivariant Schur-positivity order. **Equivariant Schur LPP inequality.**

$$
s_\lambda(\mathbf x_k; \mathbf y)s_\mu(\mathbf x_k; \mathbf y) \leq_s^{\mathrm{equiv}} s_{\lambda\vee\mu}(\mathbf x_k; \mathbf y)s_{\lambda\wedge\mu}(\mathbf x_k; \mathbf y).
$$

At $\mathbf y=\mathbf0$, this specializes to the classical LPP inequality. It has been checked for all Grassmannians in $S_n$ with $n\leq7$ and randomly for Grassmannians in $S_{10}$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Peter L. Guo, Mingyang Kang and Jiaji Liu, “A Lam–Postnikov–Pylyavskyy inequality for hybrid Grothendieck polynomials”, arXiv:2607.03116 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03116

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2026). “Hence when restricted to $k$-Grassmannians, Conjecture reduces to a statement for stable Grothendieck polynomials, as previously predicted by Thomas and Yong (see also Mihalcea ) which remains open.”

record.title: Baxter onset defect conjecture for Miura-ori boundary corrections
record.statement:
Let $E_d(m,n)$ be the count and let $p_d(m,n)$ denote its closed-form polynomial in the threshold regime. For $s=\min(m,n)<d-1$, define the boundary correction, with the other variable denoted by $n$, by

$$
B_d^{(s)}(n):=E_d(s,n)-p_d(s,n).
$$

Let $\operatorname{Bax}(k)$ be the $k$-th Baxter number. **Baxter onset defect conjecture.** For every $d\ge4$, the correction $B_d^{(d-2)}(n)$ is linear in $n$ with leading coefficient $-4\operatorname{Bax}(d-3)$. The observed coefficients agree with the first Baxter numbers, and transfer-matrix computations extend the agreement through $d=11$; a proof remains open and would show that the threshold $d-1$ is sharp.
record.source_name: Chakshu Gupta, “One construction for the Miura-ori flip-graph degree sequence”, arXiv:2607.05567 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05567

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2026). “This was verified at $d=5,6,7,8$ across $m\in\{d-1,d,d+1,d+2,d+3\}$, twenty cases in all, by exact-rational polynomial fit of $E_d(m,n)$.”

record.title: Consecutive-value conjecture for supersingular elliptic curves
record.statement: For each $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, there should exist a prime $p$ such that, for every integer $m$ with $1\leq m\leq n$, there is a supersingular elliptic curve $E$ defined over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ with $\delta_E=m$. **Consecutive-value conjecture.** For each $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, there exists a prime $p$ such that for all $1\leq m\leq n$, there is a supersingular elliptic curve $E$ defined over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ with $\delta_E=m$. The conjecture is verified in the paper for every $n\leq48$ using $p=234959$, but no general proof is given.
record.source_name: Yves Aubry, Roger Oyono and Christelle Vincent, “Minimal degree of an isogeny between a supersingular elliptic curve and its conjugate”, arXiv:2607.14624 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14624

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

record.title: Global spectral minimizer conjecture for signed circulants $C_n(1,2)$
record.statement:
Let $C_n(1,2)$ be the circulant graph on even $n$ vertices, let $A_\sigma$ range over its signed adjacency matrices, and define

$$
\rho_-(n)=2\sqrt{\cos^2(\pi/n)+\cos^2(2\pi/n)}.
$$

The switching classes are coordinatized by triangle fluxes and the Hamilton-cycle holonomy; the class with alternating triangle flux and anti-periodic step-$1$ holonomy $\alpha=-1$ has spectral radius $\rho_-(n)$. **Global minimizer conjecture.** For every even $n\ge 8$,

$$
\min_\sigma\rho(A_\sigma)=\rho_-(n).
$$

This is a flux-minimization claim in the spirit of Lieb's flux-phase theorem. Exhaustive enumeration verifies it for $n\in\{8,10,12,14,16,18\}$, but the asserted lower bound for all even $n$ remains open.
record.source_name: Vaibhav Suvagiya, “Signed circulants at the Ramanujan bound”, arXiv:2607.18334 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18334

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

record.title: Bernoulli numerator divisibility and representation by a quadratic form
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $B_{p-1}$ denote the $(p-1)$-st Bernoulli number, and let $\operatorname{num}(B_{p-1})$ denote its numerator. Consider the quadratic form

$$
F(x,y)=-x^2+2xy+2y^2.
$$

**Bernoulli–quadratic-form conjecture.** For every prime $p$,

$$
\frac{p-1}{2}\mid \operatorname{num}(B_{p-1})\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p\text{ is representable by }F(x,y).
$$

The claim connects divisibility properties of Bernoulli numbers with representation of primes by a binary quadratic form of discriminant $12$. The source presents it as a conjectural pattern, and no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Andrei R. Svinin, “On a certain arithmetic function defined via Bernoulli numbers”, arXiv:2607.18607 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18607

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

record.title: The proper hat-guessing number conjecture for two-spine book graphs
record.statement:
Let $B_{2,n}$ denote the two-spine book graph with $n$ pages, and let $\operatorname{HGP}(G)$ be the proper hat-guessing number of a graph $G$. **Two-spine book graph conjecture.** For every $n\geq4$,

$$
\operatorname{HGP}(B_{2,n})=\min\{n+3,11\}.
$$

The preceding results establish the stated values in several ranges and show stabilization at $11$ for all $n\geq n_0$. The lower bound remains open for the finite range before stabilization.
record.source_name: Yulin Zhai, “Proper Hat-Guessing on Two-Spine Book Graphs”, arXiv:2607.25274 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25274

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2026). “Its lower bound remains open for the finite range before stabilization.”

record.title: Erdős–Selfridge odd covering problem
record.statement:
A **covering system** of the integers is a finite family of congruence classes $a_i \pmod{n_i}$ whose union is all of $\mathbb{Z}$. The moduli are **odd, distinct, and greater than $1$** when every $n_i$ is odd, the moduli are pairwise distinct, and $n_i>1$ for every $i$.

**Erdős–Selfridge odd covering problem.** Does there exist a covering system of $\mathbb{Z}$ whose moduli are odd, distinct, and greater than $1$?

The problem is open in both directions and is Erdős's problem #7. An odd covering system would have consequences for the reducibility of trinomials, and the paper gives a kernel-checked exclusion showing that any such covering would have least common multiple exceeding $10000$.
record.source_name: Ibrahim Mian and Shayaan Siddique, “Kernel-Checked Exclusions for the Erdős-Selfridge Odd Covering Problem: Any Odd Covering of Z Has lcm Exceeding 10000”, arXiv:2607.25628 (2026).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2507.23041](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23041), [arXiv:1811.03547](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.03547).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25628

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2026). “The problem is open in both directions and has substantial connections elsewhere in number theory; Schinzel showed that an odd covering system would have consequences for the reducibility of trinomials.”

record.title: The slope-bound interpolation conjecture for $d$-gonal loci
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}_d(g)$ be the exact upper bound for slopes of families of stable curves with smooth $d$-gonal general member, and let $g_d=2d-3$ for $d\geq 3$ and $g_2=2$. **Slope-bound interpolation conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{F}_d(g)=6+\frac{12}{g+1}+6\frac{(1-f_d)(g-g_d)(g-1)}{(g+f_d)(g_d+1)(g+1)},
$$

or equivalently,

$$
\mathcal{F}_d(g)=6+\frac{6}{g+f_d}\left(1+f_d+\frac{1-f_d}{g_d+1}(g-1)\right).
$$

The preceding conjecture fixes the values at $g=1$ and $g=g_d$; this conjecture proposes the exact rational interpolation for all relevant genera, with the remaining factor $f_d$ discussed separately in the source. It is supported there by known hyperelliptic and trigonal results and partial tetragonal results.
record.source_name: Zvezdelina E. Stankova-Frenkel, “Moduli of Trigonal Curves”, arXiv:alg-geom/9710015 (1997).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9710015

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 1997).

record.title: Zel'manov's classification conjecture for just-infinite pro-$p$ groups of finite width
record.statement: Let $G$ be a **just-infinite pro-$p$-group of finite width**, meaning a just-infinite pro-$p$-group whose finite-index subgroup growth layers have uniformly bounded width. **Zel'manov's classification conjecture.** $G$ is either solvable, $p$-adic analytic, or commensurable to a positive part of a loop group or to the Nottingham group. This conjecture concerns the classification of just-infinite pro-$p$ groups under a finite-width hypothesis. The source presents it as a conjecture discussed by many mathematicians and stated by Zel'manov in 1996; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Laurent Bartholdi and Rostislav I. Grigorchuk, “Lie Methods in Growth of Groups and Groups of Finite Width”, arXiv:math/0002010 (2000).

record.title: Beilinson–Lichtenbaum generalized Hilbert 90 conjecture for motivic cohomology
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $n\ge 0$. The motivic complex ${\bf Z}(n)$ is evaluated on $\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ in the étale topology. **Beilinson–Lichtenbaum's generalized Hilbert 90 conjecture.** For every field $k$ and every $n\ge 0$, one has

$$
{\bf H}^{n+1}_{et}(\operatorname{Spec}(k),{\bf Z}(n))=0.
$$

This conjecture is a fundamental property expected of motivic complexes and is the main conjectural input behind the Beilinson–Lichtenbaum comparison results. The paper proves its 2-local version, but the statement as written is not resolved by the supplied text.
record.source_name: Vladimir Voevodsky, “On 2-torsion in motivic cohomology”, arXiv:math/0107110 (2001).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0107110

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2001).

record.title: Beilinson–Lichtenbaum generalized Hilbert 90 conjecture in Lichtenbaum motivic cohomology
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. For an abelian group $A$, define the Lichtenbaum motivic cohomology groups by

$$
H^{p,q}_L(X,A):={\bf H}^p_{et}(X,A\otimes {\bf Z}(q)).
$$

**Beilinson–Lichtenbaum generalized Hilbert 90 conjecture.** For every $n\ge 0$, one has

$$
H^{n+1,n}_L(\operatorname{Spec}(k),{\bf Z})=0.
$$

This is the Lichtenbaum-cohomology formulation of the generalized Hilbert 90 property and is a restatement of the earlier motivic-cohomology conjecture, so it is recorded here as the fullest formulation rather than as a separate claim.
record.source_name: Vladimir Voevodsky, “On 2-torsion in motivic cohomology”, arXiv:math/0107110 (2001).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0107110

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2001).

record.title: General algebraic-form conjecture for generating functions counting occurrences of 321
record.statement:
Let $s_n((3,2,1),r)$ denote the number of permutations of length $n$ containing exactly $r$ occurrences of the pattern $(3,2,1)$, and let

$$
F_{(3,2,1),r}(x)=\sum_{n\geq 0}s_n((3,2,1),r)x^n.
$$

For each $r$, let $P_r$ and $Q_r$ denote polynomials. **The 321 generating-function form conjecture.** For every $r$,

$$
F_{(3,2,1),r}(x)=\frac{1}{2x^{2r+1}}\left(P_r(x)+\sqrt{1-4x}\,Q_r(x)\right).
$$

This conjecture proposes a uniform algebraic form extending the displayed cases. The paper contrasts it with a corresponding result for the $(3,1,2)$ pattern, which it says was proved by Bóna; the supplied text gives no proof or resolution for the 321 assertion.
record.source_name: Markus Fulmek, “Enumeration of permutations containing a prescribed number of occurrences of a pattern of length 3”, arXiv:math/0112092 (2002).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0112092

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2001).

record.title: Explicit generating-function form conjecture for even and odd 132-occurrence counts
record.statement:
Let $E_r(x)$ and $O_r(x)$ denote the generating functions for even and odd permutations, respectively, with exactly $r$ occurrences of $132$. For every $r\geq1$, there exist polynomials $A_r(x)$, $B_r(x)$, $C_r(x)$, and $D_r(x)$ with integer coefficients such that

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_r(x)&=\frac{1}{4}(A_r(x)+B_r(x))+\frac{1}{4}C_r(x)(1-4x)^{-r+1/2}+\frac{1}{4}D_r(x)(1-4x^2)^{-r+1/2},\\
O_r(x)&=\frac{1}{4}(A_r(x)-B_r(x))+\frac{1}{4}C_r(x)(1-4x)^{-r+1/2}-\frac{1}{4}D_r(x)(1-4x^2)^{-r+1/2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

**Explicit generating-function form conjecture.** The displayed representations hold for every $r\geq1$. The paper presents this as a stronger conjecture motivated by explicit results; no proof or disproof is supplied in the given text.
record.source_name: T. Mansour, “Counting occurrences of 132 in an even permutation”, arXiv:math/0211205 (2002).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0211205

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2002).

record.title: Slope quotient principle for effective divisors on the moduli space of curves
record.statement:
Let $s_g$ be the slope of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$, and let $s(D)$ denote the slope of an effective divisor $D\equiv a\lambda-\sum_{i=0}^{[g/2]}b_i\delta_i$. **Slope quotient principle.** For every genus $g$, the following statement should hold: there exists $\epsilon_g>0$ such that any effective divisor $D$ on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$ satisfying

$$
s_g\leq s(D)\leq s_g+\epsilon_g
$$

has $s(D)=a/b_0$, equivalently $b_0\leq b_i$ for all $i\geq 1$. The theorem establishing this assertion is stated in the paper for $g\leq 23$, while the displayed sentence conjectures its validity in arbitrary genus.
record.source_name: Gavril Farkas and Mihnea Popa, “Effective divisors on M_g, curves on K3 surfaces and the Slope Conjecture”, arXiv:math/0305112 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0305112

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2003).

record.title: The short-interval prime conjecture
record.statement:
For a real number $\theta>0$ and sufficiently large $x$, the interval $[x,x+x^\theta]$ contains a prime number. **The short-interval prime conjecture.** Given $\theta>0$, for all sufficiently large $x$, the interval

$$
[x,x+x^\theta]
$$

contains a prime number. This is a conjecture from prime number theory; the source notes that it is known for all $\theta>0.525$, while the paper assumes it in proving its main theorem.
record.source_name: Ernie Croot, “A Structure Theorem for Positive Density Sets Having the Minimal Number of 3-term Arithmetic Progressions”, arXiv:math/0305318 (2003).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0305318

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2003); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Prefix-exchange conjecture for increasing and decreasing patterns
record.statement:
Let $\sigma$ and $\tau$ be patterns, and write $\sigma\sim_{\mathcal{I}}\tau$ when they are equinumerous for avoidance by involutions, meaning that $\mathcal{I}_{n}(\sigma)=\mathcal{I}_{n}(\tau)$ for every $n$. A prefix is an initial consecutive pattern such as $12\ldots k$ or $k\ldots21$. **Prefix-exchange conjecture.** For every $k$, the prefixes $12\ldots k$ and $k\ldots21$ may be exchanged; equivalently,

$$
12\ldots k\sim_{\mathcal{I}}k\ldots21.
$$

The conjecture extends the known results for short increasing and decreasing prefixes and would explain further pattern equivalences for involutions. Its general case is left open in the source.
record.source_name: Aaron D. Jaggard, “Prefix exchanging and pattern avoidance by involutions”, arXiv:math/0306002 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306002

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2003).

record.title: Symmetric-placement prefix-exchange conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a self-conjugate shape, and let $\mu_{sym}(\sigma)$ be the number of symmetric full placements on $\mu$ that avoid the pattern $\sigma$. **Symmetric-placement prefix-exchange conjecture.** For every $k$ and every self-conjugate shape $\mu$,

$$
\mu_{sym}(12\ldots k)=\mu_{sym}(k\ldots21).
$$

This is a placement-level strengthening of the prefix-exchange phenomenon for involution pattern avoidance. The source presents the assertion as a conjecture, with no resolution given there.
record.source_name: Aaron D. Jaggard, “Prefix exchanging and pattern avoidance by involutions”, arXiv:math/0306002 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306002

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2003).

record.title: The 12345–43215 involution-equivalence conjecture
record.statement:
For a pattern $\tau$, let $\mathcal{I}_{n}(\tau)$ denote the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $\tau$, and write $\sigma\sim_{\mathcal{I}}\tau$ when the two patterns have equal avoidance counts for every $n$. **12345–43215 equivalence conjecture.**

$$
12345\sim_{\mathcal{I}}43215.
$$

The assertion is one of the two pattern equivalences identified as consistent with the tabulated data for patterns of length five. The source gives no proof or later resolution in the supplied material.
record.source_name: Aaron D. Jaggard, “Prefix exchanging and pattern avoidance by involutions”, arXiv:math/0306002 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306002

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2003).

record.title: Surjectivity of the genus function for weight-2 newforms on \(\Gamma_0(N)\)
record.statement:
Let $g_0^+(N,2)$ denote the dimension of the space of weight-$2$ newforms on $\Gamma_0(N)$, equivalently the genus of the corresponding new modular curve. **Surjectivity conjecture.** For every nonnegative integer $k$, there is at least one positive integer $N$ such that

$$
g_0^+(N,2)=k.
$$

Computations for $N\le132{,}000$ found every nonnegative integer through $4{,}361$ among the values of $g_0^+(N,2)$, motivating this assertion; its validity for all $k$ remains open.
record.source_name: Greg Martin, “Dimensions of the Spaces of Cusp Forms and Newforms on Gamma_0(N) and Gamma_1(N)”, arXiv:math/0306128 (2003).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306128

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2003).

record.title: Exact lowest degree conjecture for Schur Q-functions
record.statement: Let $\lambda$ be a strict partition, and let $Q_{\lambda}$ be the Schur Q-function. Give each power sum symmetric function degree $1$, so that $\deg(p_{\nu})=\ell(\nu)$. Let $\operatorname{srank}(\lambda)$ denote the shifted rank of $\lambda$. **Exact lowest degree conjecture.** The terms of lowest degree in $Q_{\lambda}$ have degree exactly $\operatorname{srank}(\lambda)$. This strengthens the preceding lower bound on the lowest degree of $Q_{\lambda}$; it has been computationally verified for all partitions $\lambda\vdash n$ with $1\leq n\leq 12$, but no general proof is given here.
record.source_name: Peter Clifford, “Minimal Bar Tableaux”, arXiv:math/0311418 (2003).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0311418

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2003).

record.title: Miller's quadratic refinement conjecture for Sendov's problem
record.statement:
Let $S(\beta)$ be the set of polynomials of degree at least $2$ with complex coefficients, all roots in the unit disk and at least one root at $\beta$. For $P\in S(\beta)$, let $d(P,\beta)$ be the distance between $\beta$ and the closest root of $P'$, and define

$$
r(\beta)=\sup\{d(P,\beta):P\in S(\beta)\}.
$$

By rotation, assume $0\leq\beta\leq 1$. **Miller's quadratic refinement conjecture.** For every $\beta\in[0,1]$,

$$
r(\beta)\leq 1-\frac{3}{10}\beta(1-\beta).
$$

This strengthens Sendov's conjectured bound while preserving equality at the endpoints $\beta=0$ and $\beta=1$. The paper proves it for polynomials of degree $2$ or $3$, for real polynomials of degree $4$, and in several further special cases, but leaves the general assertion open.
record.source_name: Michael Miller, “The best possible quadratic refinement of Sendov's conjecture”, arXiv:math/0312130 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0312130

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2003).

record.title: Average auxiliary-count conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p$ range over primes, let $C_{a\,\mathsf{ANY},h\,\mathsf{ANY}}(p)$ be the auxiliary solution count used in the paper, let $\operatorname{Li}(x)$ be the logarithmic integral, and let $C>0$ be arbitrary.

**Average auxiliary-count conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{p\le x}\frac{C_{a\,\mathsf{ANY},h\,\mathsf{ANY}}(p)}{p-1}=2.644\cdots\operatorname{Li}(x)+O_C\left(\frac{x}{\ln^C x}\right).
$$

The numerical constant is motivated by the observed average of an auxiliary arithmetic function. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution of this conjecture.
record.source_name: Joshua Holden and Pieter Moree, “Some Heuristics and Results for Small Cycles of the Discrete Logarithm”, arXiv:math/0401013 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0401013

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2004).

record.title: Unbounded vertices conjecture for arbitrary-tree phylogenetic polytopes
record.statement: Let $T$ be a rooted tree, let ${\mathcal A}_T$ be the configuration of exponent vectors from the toric parametrization, and let $P_T$ be the convex hull of the columns of ${\mathcal A}_T$. As $T$ ranges over arbitrary trees, the number of vertices of $P_T$ should be unbounded. The paper contrasts this with the conjectured boundedness for binary trees and supports the assertion with computations, including a 15-node tree whose polytope has 34 vertices; a general proof is not supplied.
record.source_name: Nicholas Eriksson, “Toric ideals of homogeneous phylogenetic models”, arXiv:math/0401175 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0401175

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2004).

record.title: Symmetry conjecture for generating functions of even and odd 3412-avoiding involutions
record.statement:
Let $I(3412,[l_1,\ldots,l_m])$ denote the involutions under consideration, and let $F^-_{[l_1,\ldots,l_m]}(x)$ and $F^+_{[l_1,\ldots,l_m]}(x)$ be the generating functions for the odd and even involutions, respectively.

**Symmetry conjecture.** For all $m \ge 1$ and all $l_1, \ldots, l_m \ge 1$, the generating functions for the even involutions in $I(3412, [l_1, \ldots, l_m])$ and for the odd involutions in $I(3412, [l_1, \ldots, l_m])$ are symmetric in $l_1, \ldots, l_m$.

The conjecture combines the separately stated symmetry claims for $F^-_{[l_1,\ldots,l_m]}(x)$ and $F^+_{[l_1,\ldots,l_m]}(x)$. The negative case was verified computationally for $m=3$ with $l_i\le 24$ and for $m=4$ with $l_i\le 20$; the general statement remains open.
record.source_name: Eric Egge and Toufik Mansour, “Involutions Restricted by 3412, Continued Fractions, and Chebyshev Polynomials”, arXiv:math/0401217 (2004).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2003–2004). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0307050](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307050).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0401217

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2004).

record.title: Zigzag structure of direct products of polygons
record.statement:
Let $C_p$ and $C_q$ be polygons, and set

$$
t=\gcd(p,q),\qquad s=\frac{pq}{t^2}.
$$

Write $z$ for the multiset of zigzag lengths and multiplicities, and $Int$ for intersection vectors. **Product-of-polygons conjecture.** For the direct product $C_p\times C_q$: if $p,q$ are both even, then $z=(2ts)^{6t}$ with $Int=(0,2s)^t$ for every zigzag; if exactly one of $p,q$ is odd, then $z=(2ts)^{6t}$, with $Int=(0,s)^{2t}$ for $4t$ zigzags and $Int=(s,s)^t$ for the remaining $2t$ zigzags; and if $p,q$ are both odd, then $z=(2ts)^{2t},(4ts)^{2t}$, with $Int=(s,s)^t$ for zigzags of length $2ts$ and $Int=(2s,2s)^t$ for zigzags of length $4ts$. The conjecture was checked for $p,q\leq 15$; its general validity remains unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Michel Deza and Mathieu Dutour, “Zigzag structure of complexes”, arXiv:math/0405279 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405279

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2004).

record.title: Universal positive lower bound for the tau constant of metrized graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a metrized graph, with total length $\ell(\Gamma)$ and tau constant $\tau(\Gamma)$. The ratio $\tau(\Gamma)/\ell(\Gamma)$ is invariant under scaling all edge lengths by the same positive constant. **Universal lower-bound conjecture.** There is a universal constant $C>0$ such that, for all metrized graphs $\Gamma$, 

$$
\tau(\Gamma) \geq C\cdot\ell(\Gamma).
$$

The conjecture asks for a positive scale-independent lower bound for the tau constant. The source notes that the conjecture was subsequently proved by Zubeyir Cinkir, with $C=1/108$.
record.source_name: Matthew Baker and Robert Rumely, “Harmonic analysis on metrized graphs”, arXiv:math/0407427 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0407427

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2004); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The 3x+1 conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\Pi$ be the set of positive integers relatively prime to $2$ and $3$. For $x\in\Pi$, define the $(3x+1)$-Map $M$ by choosing $k\geq 1$ such that $2^k\parallel(3x+1)$ and setting

$$
y=\frac{3x+1}{2^k}.
$$

**$(3x+1)$-Conjecture.** For every $x\in\Pi$, there is an integer $n$ such that

$$
M^n(x)=1.
$$

This is the classical Collatz-type assertion that every positive integer in the natural domain of the odd-step map eventually reaches the fixed point $1$. The source reports computational verification for all $x\in\Pi$ with $0<x<2^{60}$, but the universal statement remains open.
record.source_name: Alex V. Kontorovich and Steven J. Miller, “Benford's Law, Values of L-functions and the 3x+1 Problem”, arXiv:math/0412003 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0412003

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2004).

record.title: The $4k+1$ conjecture for perfect Skolem-type sequences
record.statement:
A **perfect Skolem-type sequence of order $n$** is a sequence constructed from an ordinary perfect Skolem set of cardinality $n$. **The $4k+1$ conjecture.** For every order $n$, the number of perfect Skolem-type sequences is of the form

$$
4k+1
$$

for some integer $k$. The conjecture is suggested by the computed counts through order $13$. The observed oddness comes from reversal pairing, with one reversal-invariant sequence; the stronger congruence modulo $4$ remains presented as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Gustav Nordh, “Perfect Skolem sets”, arXiv:math/0506155 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506155

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2005). “The conjecture does not hold when we allow the sets to be multisets.”

record.title: Kühn­el–Lassmann minimality conjecture for combinatorial tori
record.statement:
Let $T^d$ be the $d$-dimensional torus, and consider the Kühn­el–Lassmann combinatorial triangulation with $2^{d+1}-1$ vertices.

**Kühn­el–Lassmann torus conjecture.** The Kühn­el–Lassmann series of combinatorial $d$-tori $T^d$ with $2^{d+1}-1$ vertices is vertex-minimal.

The series gives explicit triangulations for all $d\geq2$. The paper reports alternative $31$-vertex triangulations of $T^4$ and further triangulations in dimension $8$, but no additional $15$-vertex triangulation of $T^3$; the asserted minimality was open in the source.
record.source_name: Frank H. Lutz, “Triangulated Manifolds with Few Vertices: Combinatorial Manifolds”, arXiv:math/0506372 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506372

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2005). “It is, however, an open problem whether the $g$-theorem can be extended to general simplicial spheres (`$g$-conjecture for simplicial spheres' by McMullen ).”

record.title: The 6n alternating binomial-sum divisibility conjecture
record.statement:
For positive integers $r$, $s$, $t$, and $n$, define

$$
S_{6}(r,s,t;n)=
\sum_{k=-n}^n(-1)^k{6n\choose 3n+k}^r{4n\choose 2n+k}^s{2n\choose n+k}^t.
$$

**The 6n divisibility conjecture.** For all positive $r$, $s$, $t$, and $n$, $S_{6}(r,s,t;n)$ is divisible by both

$$
2{6n\choose n}\qquad\text{and}\qquad 6{6n\choose 3n}.
$$

This conjecture refines the preceding divisibility result, which gives divisibility by ${6n\choose n}$ and ${6n\choose 3n}$. The paper reports computational verification for $r+s+t\leq 10$ and $n\leq 100$, but no general proof is given.
record.source_name: Victor J. W. Guo, Frederic Jouhet and Jiang Zeng, “Factors of Alternating Sums of Products of Binomial and q-Binomial Coefficients”, arXiv:math/0511635 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0511635

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2005).

record.title: Automorphic matrix-coefficient bound for low-rank absolutely almost simple groups
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a global field, let $\mathbf G$ be a connected absolutely almost simple $K$-group, and let $W_f$ be a compact open subgroup of $\mathbf G(\bA_f)$. For $f,h\in L^2_{00}(\mathbf G(K)\backslash \mathbf G(\bA))$, assume that $f$ and $h$ are $U_\infty\times W_f$-invariant unit vectors. **Automorphic bound.** There is a constant $c_{W_f}>0$, depending only on $\mathbf G$ and $W_f$, such that

$$
|\langle f,g.h\rangle|\leq c_{W_f}\cdot \xi_{\mathbf G}(g)
$$

for all $g\in \mathbf G(\bA)$. This conjectural estimate would provide uniform decay of matrix coefficients for the automorphic spectrum in $L^2_{00}$, particularly when the $K$-rank is at most one, where the corresponding bound for arbitrary infinite-dimensional representations does not generally hold.
record.source_name: Alex Gorodnik, Francois Maucourant and Hee Oh, “Manin's and Peyre's conjectures on rational points and adelic mixing”, arXiv:math/0601127 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601127

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2006).

record.title: Casson–Gordon's three-family conjecture for 2-bridge ribbon knots
record.statement:
A **2-bridge ribbon knot** is a ribbon knot that is also a 2-bridge knot. Casson and Gordon identified three families of 2-bridge ribbon knots.

**Casson–Gordon's conjecture.** Every 2-bridge ribbon knot is contained in one of the three families of Casson and Gordon.

The conjecture is supported computationally: it was verified for all 2-bridge knots with determinant at most $571^2$, including all such knots with crossing number at most $26$. A proof remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Christoph Lamm, “Symmetric union presentations for 2-bridge ribbon knots”, arXiv:math/0602395 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602395

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2006).

record.title: The power-of-two conjecture for skew-equivalence classes
record.statement:
A **skew diagram** is a finite diagram of cells arranged in the usual skew Young-diagram shape, and two skew diagrams are **skew-equivalent** when they have the same skew Schur function. For a skew diagram $D$, write $[D]$ for its skew-equivalence class.

**Power-of-two conjecture.** Every skew-equivalence class of skew diagrams has cardinality a power of $2$.

The conjecture is motivated by the observed pairing of skew-equivalences in the examples displayed in the paper and was verified there for all skew diagrams with up to $18$ cells.
record.source_name: Victor Reiner, Kristin M. Shaw and Stephanie van Willigenburg, “Coincidences among skew Schur functions”, arXiv:math/0602634 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602634

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2006).

record.title: The averaged symmetrization inequality for Rayleigh partition functions
record.statement:
Let $Z(\omega;\mathbf y)$ be Rayleigh, and let $\widetilde Z$ be its symmetrization. For each $e\in E$ and each pair $\{e,f\}\subseteq E$, use the auxiliary quantities $z(e)$ and $z(ef)$ defined from the symmetrized derivatives in the source. **Averaged symmetrization inequality.** For every $\mathbf y>\boldsymbol 0$,

$$
\sum_{\{e,f\}\subseteq E}\bigl(z(e)z(f)-z(ef)\widetilde Z^{12}\bigr)\geq0.
$$

The inequality is presented as a sufficient condition for the symmetrization conjecture and is not proved in the paper.
record.source_name: David G. Wagner, “Negatively correlated random variables and Mason's conjecture”, arXiv:math/0602648 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602648

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2006). “A positive solution to the Big Conjecture would be a very good thing.”

record.title: The pairwise symmetrization inequality for Rayleigh partition functions
record.statement:
Let $Z(\omega;\mathbf y)$ be Rayleigh, let $\widetilde Z$ be its symmetrization, and let $z(e)$ and $z(ef)$ be the auxiliary quantities defined in the source. **Pairwise symmetrization inequality.** For every pair $\{e,f\}\subseteq E$ and every $\mathbf y>\boldsymbol 0$,

$$
z(e)z(f)-z(ef)\widetilde Z^{12}\geq0.
$$

This is described as a simpler and stronger sufficient conjecture for the preceding averaged inequality, hence for the symmetrization conjecture; it remains open.
record.source_name: David G. Wagner, “Negatively correlated random variables and Mason's conjecture”, arXiv:math/0602648 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602648

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2006). “A positive solution to the Big Conjecture would be a very good thing.”

record.title: The irreducibility conjecture for the numerator of the binary-form Poincaré series
record.statement:
Let $n\ge3$, and write the Poincaré series in lowest terms as

$$
P_n(t)=\frac{A_n(t)}{B_n(t)},
$$

where $A_n,B_n\in\mathbf Z[t]$ are relatively prime and $A_n(0)=B_n(0)=1$. **Irreducibility conjecture.** The polynomial $A_n(t)$ is irreducible for every $n\ge5$. The paper presents this as an additional conjecture after reporting computations through $n=30$; no general proof is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Dragomir Ž. Djoković, “A heuristic algorithm for computing the Poincaré series of the invariants of binary forms”, arXiv:math/0608147 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608147

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

record.title: The low-genus Kodaira-dimension conjecture for $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$
record.statement:
Let $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$ be the moduli space of stable curves of genus $g$, and let $\kappa(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g)$ denote its Kodaira dimension. **Low-genus Kodaira-dimension conjecture.**

$$
\kappa(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g)=-\infty\quad\text{for all }g<23.
$$

This statement is presented as an immediate consequence of the slope conjecture. The general-type threshold is known to begin at $g\geq 24$, but the asserted negative Kodaira dimension for every $g<23$ remains the conjectural part in the source.
record.source_name: Gavril Farkas, “The global geometry of the moduli space of curves”, arXiv:math/0612251 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0612251

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2006).

record.title: The corrected Welsh conjecture on the possible numbers of matroid bases
record.statement:
Let $n$ and $r$ be integers, and let $b$ be the number of bases of a matroid of rank $r$ on $n$ elements. The necessary bounds are

$$
1 \leq b \leq \binom{n}{r}.
$$

**Corrected Welsh conjecture.** For every triple $(n,r,b)$ such that $0 \leq r \leq n$ and $1 \leq b \leq \binom{n}{r}$, there is a matroid of rank $r$ on $n$ elements with exactly $b$ bases, except when

$$
(n,r,b)=(6,3,11).
$$

The database computation found no other missing triples for $n\leq 9$, motivating this corrected formulation; the conjecture remains open beyond the computed range.
record.source_name: Dillon Mayhew and Gordon F. Royle, “Matroids with nine elements”, arXiv:math/0702316 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0702316

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2007).

record.title: Strictification conjecture for weak sections of a left Quillen presheaf
record.statement:
Let $Y$ be a small category and let $\mathbf{M}$ be a left Quillen presheaf on $Y$. Suppose that $\mathbf{M}$ satisfies hypothesis (o), introduced in Section 19, which in particular says that each $\mathbf{M}(y)$ admits all small limits. Say that the weak sections of $\mathbf{M}$ over $Y$ strictify when the morphism

$$
Sect(Y,\int_Y\mathbf{M})\longrightarrow Sect(Y,\int'_Y L(\mathbf{M}))
$$

is essentially surjective. **Strictification conjecture.** The weak sections of $\mathbf{M}$ over $Y$ strictify in this sense. The text proves the corresponding assertion for a Reedy category and leaves the extension to an arbitrary category, under hypothesis (o), as a conjecture.
record.source_name: André Hirschowitz and Carlos Simpson, “Descente pour les n-champs (Descent for n-stacks)”, arXiv:math/9807049 (2001).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9807049

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 1998).

record.title: The congruence ABC conjecture for $N$
record.statement:
Let $N$ be an integer. An **ABC-solution** is a triple $\mathbf{s}=(a,b,c)$ of distinct relatively prime integers satisfying $a+b+c=0$, with $a$ and $b$ negative. For $n>0$, define $\operatorname{rad}(n)$ as the product of all primes dividing $n$, and set

$$
f(\mathbf{s},\epsilon)=\log(c)-(1+\epsilon)\log \operatorname{rad}(abc).
$$

**Congruence ABC conjecture for $N$.** For each $\epsilon>0$, there exists a constant $C_\epsilon$ such that

$$
f(\mathbf{s},\epsilon)<C_\epsilon
$$

for all ABC-solutions $\mathbf{s}$ such that $N\mid abc$. These are weaker, congruence-restricted versions of the ABC conjecture. The source explains that Oesterlé had shown the case $N=16$ implies the full ABC conjecture and proposes the family for every integer $N$; no resolution status is supplied here.
record.source_name: Jordan S. Ellenberg, “Congruence ABC implies ABC”, arXiv:math/9909098 (1999).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9909098

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 1999).
